PullRequest.Title: editor: place the cursor on clicks between the folding chevron and the text
PullRequest.Body:

Refs #135114 (and its duplicate #206914)

## Problem

The line decorations area between the line numbers and the text is 26px wide by default: 10px for decorations such as the SCM quick diff bar, plus 16px for folding. Clicks in this area never place the cursor, and the folding control is rendered across almost all of it. So clicking just left of the first character either toggles a fold or does nothing, and only the first pixel of the text places the cursor at column 1.

## Change

A click in the line decorations area now behaves like a click on the content left of the text, unless it lands on a rendered line decoration. The browser's hit test decides, so the code doesn't need to know any decoration's position or size:

- `MouseTargetFactory._hitTestMargin` returns `CONTENT_EMPTY` at the start of the line (the end of the line for RTL text) when the mouse target is not a line decoration element (`.cldr`, rendered by `LinesDecorationsOverlay`).
- `folding.css` makes the folding control take clicks only on its chevron. The control's box spans the whole area, so it gets `pointer-events: none`, and an invisible `::after` as wide as the chevron (10/16 of the icon, centered like the icon) takes the clicks. The rendering is unchanged.
- On mouse move, `MouseHandler` toggles the existing `monaco-mouse-cursor-text` class on the margin while the target is such a margin click (and `editor.mouseStyle` is `text`), so the pointer is an I-beam exactly where a click places the cursor, and stays a hand over the chevron. For this, `IPointerHandlerHelper` gains `marginDomNode`.

Because the DOM decides, wrapped fold-start lines (the chevron is rendered on the first row), the inline comments layout (which shifts the chevron right), the comments "+" button, font sizes and product icon themes need no special handling. Consumers of `GUTTER_LINE_DECORATIONS` (folding, SCM quick diff, comments, drag and drop) are unchanged and still get gutter targets for clicks on their decorations.

## Reviewer notes

- Lines with SCM quick diff changes behave as on `main`. The `.dirty-diff-glyph` element spans the whole area (with a hand pointer when the gutter action is enabled), so clicks there remain gutter clicks. Giving that element a box only as wide as its bar would extend this fix to modified lines; this PR leaves SCM's styles unchanged.
- Right-clicking the area now opens the editor context menu, like right-clicking left of the text. This area had no gutter context menu before (the gutter menu is for line numbers and the glyph margin).
- The `CONTENT_EMPTY` detail omits `horizontalDistanceToText`, so hovering the area does not trigger the content hover for the first word.
- Pure CSS padding (`.lines-content { padding-left }`) and `editor.lineDecorationsWidth` remain unclickable. The `editor.contentLeftPadding` setting requested in #135114 is not part of this PR.

## How to test

1. Open a file with foldable regions and set `"editor.showFoldingControls": "always"`.
2. Hover and click the chevron: the pointer is a hand, and clicking folds and unfolds.
3. Hover between the chevron and the text, or left of the chevron: the pointer is an I-beam, and clicking puts the cursor at column 1 of that line. Dragging from there selects.
4. On empty lines and lines without a chevron, the whole area behaves like step 3.
5. With `"editor.wordWrap": "on"` and a long fold-start line, the chevron still folds, and clicking the area next to a wrapped row puts the cursor at the start of that row.
6. On a line with a quick diff bar, clicking the bar still opens the quick diff peek.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/editor/browser/controller/mouseHandler.ts src/vs/editor/browser/controller/mouseTarget.ts src/vs/editor/browser/view.ts`: passed
- `node build/stylelint.ts src/vs/editor/contrib/folding/browser/folding.css`: passed
- No unit test: the behavior comes from the browser's hit test of the rendered margin, and the test editor does not render a view.
- Manual: drove a dev build of Code OSS over CDP with real mouse moves and clicks at measured offsets, reading the computed pointer before each click:
  - Default layout (12px font): the chevron folds with a hand pointer. Left and right of it, and anywhere on empty lines, the pointer is an I-beam and clicks place the cursor at column 1. Dragging from the gap selects.
  - Wrapped fold-start line: the chevron folds; the gap places the cursor at column 1, and the area next to the wrapped row places it at the start of that row.
  - Inline comments layout (`lineDecorationsWidth` 23 plus the `margin-left: 11px` that `review.css` applies to the chevron): the chevron folds, including its right part, and the area right of it places the cursor.
  - 14px font: the chevron folds and the area right of it places the cursor.
  - Modified lines: git doesn't compute quick diff changes for an unfocused window, so I added an element with the quick diff decoration's classes and box, styled by the real SCM CSS. The bar and the area right of it behave as on `main`, and the chevron on a modified fold line still folds.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The native mousemove listener, new branch, uncached getDecorationsOnLine call, and per-decoration reconstruction are directly traced. Bracket colorization provides a concrete collection-scaling trigger even with warm render caches; the duration on a particular machine is not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Bracket/decorations enumeration, recreated model-decoration/options objects, result arrays, and InlineDecoration objects.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For M delivered mousemoves over the same eligible gutter area and D decorations intersecting the queried line, the added processing and allocation are O(M × D), including on warm caches. The unwrapped-line case queries the whole line; there is no per-line result coalescing or mousemove throttling in this path.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional synchronous renderer CPU work and temporary allocations on every qualifying mousemove can cause input latency and frame drops on decoration-dense lines.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The same gutter movements returned GUTTER_LINE_DECORATIONS after the existing position/range calculation. They did not call getTextDirection, enumerate bracket decorations, or rebuild inline-decoration collections.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Ordinary movement over the empty line-decoration gutter now synchronously calls getTextDirection, which collects and processes all decorations for the view line before returning the mouse target.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call to ctx.isRtl(lineNumber) at mouseTarget.ts:730 runs in the new decoration-free margin branch. Previously _hitTestMargin returned fulfillMargin directly without querying text direction or collecting line decorations. MouseHandler._onMouseMove invokes this hit test for every delivered mousemove, including repeated movements over the same line.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding line decorations on every margin mousemove
Findings.Impact: With an unwrapped generated/minified JSON or source line containing thousands of colored brackets, moving the pointer through the decoration-free gutter repeatedly walks those brackets and rebuilds decoration arrays on the renderer thread, increasing CPU/GC pressure and delaying input and painting even when the document is unchanged.
Findings.Evidence: HitTestContext.isRtl delegates to ViewModel.getTextDirection (mouseTarget.ts:370-371). ViewModelImpl.getTextDirection calls _decorations.getDecorationsOnLine and then scans the result (viewModelImpl.ts:859-880). getDecorationsOnLine bypasses the viewport cache and calls InlineModelDecorationsComputer.getDecorations every time (viewModelDecorations.ts:69-81); that method re-queries the model, builds result arrays, and creates InlineDecoration objects (inlineDecorations.ts:92-164). TextModel.getDecorationsInRange also invokes ColorizedBracketPairsDecorationProvider, which recreates decoration/options objects for every bracket in the range (textModel.ts:1826-1832; colorizedBracketPairsDecorationProvider.ts:45-69). The existing conversion cache does not eliminate these enumerations or allocations.
Findings.Recommendation: Avoid recomputing direction from the full decoration collection for each mousemove. Expose/reuse the rendered line's already-computed direction (ViewLine.isRenderedRTL exists), or cache the authoritative direction in the view-model lifecycle with invalidation on decoration and line-mapping changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move the mouse over decoration-free line-decoration gutter, including beside long unwrapped generated/minified lines.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each native mousemove synchronously enters MouseHandler._onMouseMove, creates a target, reaches the added _hitTestMargin branch, computes direction, toggles the cursor class, and emits the event. The new decoration collection must finish before target delivery and renderer input handling can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read editor bounding rectangle and offset dimensions through browser geometry APIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lazily cached editor-position/relative-coordinate calculation per event; unchanged from before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same mousemove target construction already requested editorPos and relativePos.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous geometry reads precede target construction, but the diff does not add another geometry calculation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query in-memory model decoration providers, including bracket enumeration and projection into inline-decoration collections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new complete line-direction query per qualifying margin hit test, processing D decorations even with warm conversion/render caches; not a subprocess, database, or network request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same margin movements returned fulfillMargin without this query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All query, reconstruction, and direction-scanning CPU work is synchronous before the mouse target is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Toggle an inherited browser cursor style through the margin DOM class.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One toggle call per ordinary mousemove, with actual class changes only when the forced boolean changes; removal on mouse leave.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The margin cursor class was not toggled by mouse movement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cursor-style changes may require browser style resolution; no new unconditional geometry read follows in the changed handler itself.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M delivered mousemoves and D decorations intersecting the queried line. For an unwrapped line this includes the entire line's colored brackets and find decorations, not just visible columns. Thousands of brackets on a generated JSON/source line are supported; bracket AST construction permits documents up to 5,000,000 characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial renderer-main-thread execution for each delivered event. EditorMouseEventFactory.onMouseMove registers a direct listener with no application-level throttling or coalescing. Active selection causes the ordinary _onMouseMove path to return early and is not included in this finding's multiplicity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-event editor coordinates are memoized. The viewport decoration collection is cached, but getTextDirection uses getDecorationsOnLine, which bypasses that cache. The conversion cache reuses ViewModelDecoration instances but does not cache model queries, bracket-decoration/options reconstruction, result arrays, InlineDecoration allocation, or the final direction scan. Warm unchanged lines therefore repeat the added O(D) work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event path, added direction query, uncached aggregation, bracket-provider allocations, and synchronous execution are directly established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. Impact depends on decoration density, delivered event frequency, and renderer hardware; severity is medium rather than assuming ordinary short lines are slow.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one introduced repeated-work regression at mouseTarget.ts:730. The new O(M × D) processing/allocation persists on warm caches. The cursor-class update alone is bounded and not a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct an editor and render/scroll folding controls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: View construction already creates and attaches the margin before registering PointerHandler. The added helper field stores that existing element. Browser style/layout paints one added hit-test pseudo-element for each rendered folding control.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser constructs/styles the narrow absolute-positioned pseudo-element used for chevron hit testing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pseudo-element for each currently rendered folding-decoration element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Folding decoration elements themselves supplied the full-width hit area, without this pseudo-element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of ordinary rendering/hit testing; adds a small bounded box, with no new JavaScript layout loop or synchronous geometry query.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One margin reference per editor and one ::after pseudo-element per rendered folding chevron. LinesDecorationsOverlay prepares only the visible view-line range; cost is not proportional to every fold in a large document.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer thread with existing render scheduling and browser style/layout. No new asynchronous task, process, queue, or resource creation burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing overlay rendered-content equality suppresses unchanged line reconstruction. No new application cache or unbounded collection is introduced; pseudo-elements follow their existing decoration elements.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the new reference shares the existing view lifetime and pseudo-elements are bounded by rendered decorations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The small per-visible-icon rendering increment is unmeasured; no concrete scaling or lifecycle defect was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate reportable regression. There is no new margin subtree, leaked owner, document-wide DOM expansion, or I/O on construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click or drag from the newly enabled empty gutter area to place the cursor or select text.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The target becomes CONTENT_EMPTY and enters the existing focus/MouseDownOperation/navigation-command path. Selection changes and rendering are local; extension-host property notifications do not require a response before the cursor can move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send changed editor properties/selections to the extension host with $acceptEditorPropertiesChanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped notification per effective property update; unchanged selections/ranges are suppressed. No per-line fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A click in an undecorated gutter gap did not place the cursor, so did not cause this selection notification. Ordinary text clicks/drags already used the identical notification path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication follows local state changes and does not await extension-host completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initial click, followed by delivered drag events and the existing number of selections. Direction testing added to initial target creation also shares the reported issue, but active dragging already uses _getPositionOutsideEditor and its pre-existing direction lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active mouse-down operation and its pointer monitor per editor; renderer commands execute serially. Property IPC is fire-and-forget and grouped into one delta, not one message per selected line or decoration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MainThreadTextEditorProperties.generateDelta compares selection/options/visible-range state and emits only changed properties. If document changes have not reached the extension host, property updates are deferred until content synchronization catches up.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for target routing, existing selection operation ownership, and delta-based IPC suppression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of selection updates depends on drag motion and existing event delivery. No excessive new fan-out beyond the intended interaction was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: enabling cursor placement intentionally reaches the existing selection path. Its IPC is grouped, asynchronous, and not amplified per decoration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Right-click the newly content-like gutter gap to open the editor context menu.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ContextMenuController accepts CONTENT_EMPTY, focuses/positions the cursor if needed, obtains menu actions, and calls the existing context-menu service. HTML menus render locally; native desktop menus serialize the menu and send one popup request to the main process.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert menu entries/submenus into a serializable native-menu tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One O(A) tree conversion per native menu opening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The undecorated gutter gap did not open an editor context menu. Existing content right-clicks already performed this same conversion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before requesting the native popup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ipcRenderer.send(CONTEXT_MENU_CHANNEL, ...) requests a native context-menu popup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request containing the complete menu per native opening, with existing close/click callbacks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No popup request for a gap right-click; identical single-request behavior already existed for content right-clicks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Native display follows the request; no per-entry IPC or renderer-side synchronous wait is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and lay out an HTML menu when using the browser/custom context-menu implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One menu and its A action entries per opening, disposed by existing context-view lifetime management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No editor menu in the gap; the same HTML rendering path was used by normal content context menus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Menu DOM work is required to display the explicitly requested menu.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One menu per user context-menu gesture and A contributed menu/submenu entries. Any changed selection has the delta-notification behavior described in the cursor scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous menu-building pass and one native popup request per opening, not one IPC per action. The service's existing menu ownership/disposal behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The HTML context-menu handler is created lazily and reused. Menu actions are obtained for the current context on each explicit opening. No new persistent cache is introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both HTML and native service implementations were traced through the popup serialization and IPC send.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu size depends on contributed actions, but the PR does not change action cardinality or batching.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: this is intentional exposure of the existing menu operation on a new click target, without increased per-opening fan-out or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover/click an actual folding chevron or another rendered gutter decoration, including SCM-covered lines.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser hit testing selects the chevron's pseudo-element and reports its existing .cldr owner, or selects another decoration. The unchanged GUTTER_LINE_DECORATIONS path reaches folding/SCM consumers. Folding uses the existing local folding model and view update.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target per event. Folding a region changes its existing region set; shift/alt recursive behavior retains the pre-diff cardinality. A full-area SCM decoration continues to exclude the new empty-gutter branch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing serial input dispatch and folding/view-model updates; no new per-region asynchronous tasks or process fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing folding-model and overlay lifecycle is unchanged. The added class-membership test is constant work; rendered decoration targets do not invoke the new direction query.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: .cldr ownership is established by LinesDecorationsOverlay, and FoldingController's mouse handlers and local toggleCollapseState path are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser hit-test box overhead is unmeasured and already accounted for in the rendering scenario; no new external I/O boundary was found in the changed folding routing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. Actual decorations retain their old consumer paths; only the narrow hit box and empty surrounding area's classification change.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all four changed files and every diff page against base 7048d2809efc3c54021b0ca358d589dfc987acbf. Submitted one medium-severity, high-confidence finding for newly repeated uncached decoration reconstruction during empty-gutter mouse movement. Examined rendering/lifetimes, cursor selection and extension-host IPC, native/HTML context menus, and actual decoration interactions. No changed subprocess, filesystem, database, or network calls were found. No concrete performance-regression fix/provenance signal qualified.
